score_rationale: The paper delivers a technically substantial and carefully scoped minimax frontier, but its journal contribution is obscured by weak comparison with the closest literature, excessive duplication, an overbroad verification disclosure, and several important presentation inconsistencies.
summary: The paper characterizes minimax absolute risk and uniformly honest expected length for a deterministic continuous-treatment clamp, obtaining the frontier n^{-1/2}+δ_n^{κ+1}h_n^β and a continuity-only analogue. The verified results support the central rate, phase diagram, stabilized procedures, and exact transport to the declared causal class. Publication would require substantial restructuring, sharper positioning, and correction of the verification, typing, and criterion-level presentation issues identified below.
strengths: The central statistical contribution is precise and nontrivial: matching estimation and honest-length bounds are established across moving-threshold regimes.

The paper states its finite-stratum, bounded-outcome, Hölder-smoothness, polynomial-thinning, and oracle-knowledge conditions prominently and generally represents them faithfully in the abstract and introduction.
The total-Gram construction handles empty and singular realized local designs explicitly, an important feature often suppressed in nonparametric procedure descriptions.
The distinction between the bandwidth edge and the risk critical threshold is useful and clearly summarized in the phase table and one-cell calibration.
The causal contribution is appropriately framed as an exact transport result for the paper-defined full-data class rather than as an independently derived longitudinal frontier.
The theorem-local disclosures for the cited conditional-distribution and Hoeffding inputs correctly identify the scope of those external ingredients.

findings.issue: The dedicated section cites broad literatures but does not engage the closest competing results closely enough to substantiate novelty. In particular, it omits or barely distinguishes recent natural-value LMTP extensions, support-violation decompositions, stochastic or support-restricted threshold-response targets, and recent continuous-dose frontier results. The sentence “The resulting analysis characterizes this coupled sampling problem” therefore rests on an asserted rather than demonstrated literature boundary.
findings.fix: Add a focused comparison covering Díaz et al. (2026), Koo et al. (2026), van der Laan, Zhang, and Gilbert (2023), Donovan, Hudgens, and Gilbert (2019), and Bonvini and Kennedy (2026), along with the most relevant recent LMTP applications. For each, state its estimand, overlap or support condition, inferential result, and why its rate does not already cover the exact deterministic clamp with a moving Dirac mass. Also state Gaïffas’s rate explicitly and show how atom weighting changes that benchmark.

findings.issue: The author footnote claims that “The displayed formal statements and proofs are Lean-verified,” while the verification note and contract distinguish kernel-checked declarations from presentation-synthesized restatements and from separately audited manuscript proof narratives. The blanket sentence overstates what kernel checking covers.
findings.fix: Rewrite the footnote to say that designated anchored declarations are kernel checked, that identified reader-facing restatements are presentation synthesized, and that correspondence of displayed statements and proof narratives to the declarations is a separate audit. Preserve the theorem-local qualifications for published inputs.

findings.issue: The manuscript repeatedly defines the same objects: the model classes, clamp target, total-Gram estimator, and interval each appear in both synthesized and authoritative environments. The long theorem-local constant lists and two extensive proof appendices further obscure the core econometric argument. A reader cannot readily tell which definition is canonical or which technical details are essential to the contribution.
findings.fix: Retain one canonical environment for each object, replace duplicate environments with short cross-references, consolidate regime conditions into a single standing assumption, and move low-level measure, matrix, and verification details to a clearly labeled supplementary appendix. Keep the main text focused on the estimand, rate mechanism, procedures, lower-bound experiments, and causal transport.

findings.issue: The proposed sharp-constant program compares the full-target honest length with W_{n,B_n}, although W_{n,B_n} is an unweighted supremum of stratumwise local-regression radii. The clamp frontier also contains the retained-mean term, atom-mass uncertainty, atom weights, and cross-stratum aggregation. In regular and zero-threshold regimes, the local radius and the full frontier are generally on different scales, so the three asserted candidate matching ratios are not motivated by the preceding results. The surrounding prose itself acknowledges these omitted components.
findings.fix: Either remove the three matching-ratio conjectures and present W_{n,B_n} solely as a local ingredient, or first define a genuine target-level modulus that includes the retained mean, atom-mass terms, δ-dependent atom weights, and aggregation across strata. Pose sharp-constant limits separately by threshold regime unless a common normalization is justified.

findings.issue: The full-data class declares g_x:[0,1]×U→[0,1], but the continuity causal bridge subsequently says “for each x and a∈R, define” m_x^F(a) using g_x(a,U). As written, that expression is not typed outside [0,1]. The underlying formal representation uses a total real-domain map with its range restriction imposed on admissible doses, so the manuscript presentation is internally inconsistent.
findings.fix: Align all full-data definitions with one domain convention. The cleanest correction is to declare g_x on R×U, require joint measurability and [0,1]-valuedness on doses in [0,1], and retain potential outcomes only on the policy-relevant interval. Alternatively, restrict every definition of m_x^F to a∈[0,1].

findings.issue: The minimax-risk theorem writes the stabilized risk as an expectation under P rather than P^{⊗n}, although the estimator is a function of the n-observation sample and all surrounding definitions use the product law. In addition, the displayed definition of R_n^⋆ ranges over all measurable estimators, whereas the verified criterion and later causal comparison use [0,1]-valued estimators.
findings.fix: Replace the theorem’s expectation by E_{P^{⊗n}}. State consistently that the infimum ranges over [0,1]-valued estimators, or add a short projection lemma showing explicitly that allowing arbitrary real-valued estimators leaves the criterion unchanged.

findings.issue: The zero-threshold theorem says the stabilized risk and length are “both asymptotic to n^{-1/2}.” The verified conclusion is two-sided comparability, expressed by an asymptotic-order relation, rather than convergence of the ratio to one.
findings.fix: Replace “asymptotic to” with “of order n^{-1/2}” or “comparable to n^{-1/2}” everywhere this conclusion is described.

findings.issue: The global envelope c_-a^κ≤π_x(a)≤c_+a^κ on the entire treatment interval is substantially stronger than a local regular-variation or boundary-overlap condition. The manuscript identifies it as analysis-specific but gives little substantive motivation or explanation of which conclusions use its global rather than local form.
findings.fix: Explain the role of the lower and upper bounds in the Gram control, atom-mass comparison, and lower-bound construction; give representative treatment distributions satisfying the condition; and distinguish this global class from the local degenerate-design assumptions in the cited literature. Keep any broader-envelope extension in the open-questions discussion unless proved.

findings.issue: The sharp-constant material occupies a very large formal definition and remark despite being unresolved and peripheral to the proved rate contribution. Its notation introduces exactHolderBias, realizedExactModulus, W_{n,B_n}, several witness sequences, and multiple limit conjectures after the paper has already presented an extensive technical apparatus.
findings.fix: Condense the main-text discussion to a short target-level open question and move the realized-design definitions and candidate experiments to a supplement. Retain an explicit statement that the current object is a local half-length ingredient.

findings.issue: The notation alternates between expectations under the full-data product law and under the product law of the observed margin. These are equivalent for observed-sample procedures, but the switching makes the decision-problem equivalence harder to parse.
findings.fix: Choose one convention throughout, preferably expectations under (P^F_obs)^{⊗n}, and state once that this equals integration of any observed-measurable procedure under the full-data product law.

questions_for_authors: Which existing result do the authors regard as the closest rate benchmark: degenerate-design point regression, regular LMTP inference, or support-restricted threshold-response inference, and what exact estimand-level distinction prevents that result from covering the present clamp?

Is the intended publication artifact the econometric argument or a complete human-readable rendering of the formal development? If the former, can the duplicate definitions and low-level verified lemmas be moved to a supplement?
What atom-weighted target-level modulus is intended to replace the unweighted stratumwise radius in the sharp-constant question, particularly at δ_n=0 and in the regular regime?
Do the authors intend structural response maps to be total functions on R, as in the formal representation, or functions defined only on the treatment support [0,1]?
